jobs.title: Materials Engineer, Rocket Motor Systems
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

Anduril's Rocket Motor Systems (RMS) team is rebuilding U.S. domestic production capacity for solid rocket propulsion. We're looking for a Materials and Process (M&P) Engineer to help connect how a motor is formulated, tested, and built to how it actually performs. You'll work across the full stack of solid rocket motor materials: insulation, seals, propellants, motor cases, nozzles, and energetic systems.

About the Role

This is a role you'll grow into. Alongside a supportive team, you'll help build the M&P infrastructure that lets the RMS team scale from prototype development to high-rate production, contributing to the material specifications, process specifications, acceptance test procedures, and design allowables that turn fast-moving development work into clear, configuration-controlled engineering documentation. You'll take on more ownership as you go, and you'll have experienced engineers around you to learn from while you do.

We're looking for someone with solid materials-science fundamentals for aerospace applications, a habit of documenting their work so others can build on it, and genuine curiosity about how materials behave in the real world. You might be early in your career or already deep in it, either way, you like being hands-on in the lab and thinking about how to make good work repeatable.

What You'll Do

• Connect polymeric material properties, characterization, and processing fundamentals to solid rocket motor design, formulation, testing, manufacturing, and performance

• Build and maintain material specifications that connect system performance requirements to formulation for polymeric materials spanning raw materials, components, and assemblies, including liners, seals, propellants, cases (metal and composite), ablatives, insulators, adhesives, and coatings

• Develop standard testing procedures to characterize the mechanical, viscoelastic, thermal, and surface behavior of polymeric materials across solid rocket motor components and assemblies

• Create process specifications for manufacturing operations including propellant processing, ablative manufacturing, insulation/liner bonding and surface preparation, surface modification, coating application, adhesive curing, heat treatment, and final assembly

• Run materials characterization for polymeric materials including mechanical testing (tensile, shear, flexural, bonding), thermal analysis, rheology, cure kinetics, surface energy and interfaces, and ablation performance

• Develop design allowables from characterization results per industry standards (CMH-17, JANNAF)

• Partner with design and manufacturing teams to review drawings and manufacturing plans, support design reviews, and troubleshoot production issues

• Work across science, engineering, manufacturing, quality, and program teams to turn mission requirements into right-sized material and process solutions

• Contribute to cost-reduction and cycle-time improvement efforts for high-rate production and prepare technical documentation that lets us move fast without losing rigor

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Materials Science, Polymer Engineering, Polymer Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related field

• 2+ years of materials and process engineering experience in material testing for aerospace, propulsion, or defense applications

• Working knowledge in one or more of the following (with interest in growing into the others): polymer mechanics and rheology, propellant materials and processing, adhesive bonding, cure kinetics, and surface preparation

• Exposure to developing material or process specifications

• Experience with material characterization, testing, and documentation

• Strong technical writing and attention to detail

• Ability to manage multiple priorities independently in a fast-paced environment

• Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

• Master's or Doctorate in Materials Science, Polymer Engineering, Polymer Science, Chemical Engineering, or a related field

• Direct experience with materials used in solid rocket motors, including insulation, seals, propellants, motor cases, nozzles, and energetic components

• Depth or growing interest in two or more of the following: high-temperature coatings, adhesives, insulation, liners, and ablatives; polymer surface characterization and modification; interfacial mechanics, chemistry, and behavior (polymer-to-polymer, metal-to-polymer, ceramic-to-polymer)

• Hands-on experience with polymer processing, propellant processing, composite fabrication, ablative manufacturing, or metal case production

• Experience developing design allowables per CMH-17, JANNAF, or MIL-HDBK-17 standards

• Experience with NDI methods and developing inspection procedures

• Experience characterizing polymer material interfaces across solid rocket motor systems (insulation-to-propellant, insulation-to-motor case, seals-to-motor case) via mechanical, thermal, and/or spectroscopy methods

• Familiarity with MIL-STDs, AIAA standards, and JANNAF best practices

• Knowledge of rocket motor design, internal ballistics, and combustion environments

• Experience participating in Engineering Review Boards, Material Review Boards, and Failure Review Boards

• Experience transitioning processes from development to production in agile environments

US Salary Range

$87,000—$116,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

jobs.title: Veterinary Laboratory Technician

Veterinary Laboratory Technician

Compensation: $24 - $27 per hour, based on experience and qualifications

VERG Brooklyn is looking for an experienced Veterinary Laboratory Technician to join our team. You’ll perform diagnostic testing, manage laboratory equipment, and deliver the accurate, timely results our medical teams rely on to make important treatment decisions.

If you’re detail-oriented, enjoy hands-on laboratory work, and stay focused in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us

Your work has an immediate impact: Every sample tells part of a patient’s story. The results you provide will help our veterinarians diagnose conditions, determine treatment plans, and respond quickly during emergency cases.

You’ll be part of the medical team: Although much of your work takes place behind the scenes, your role is essential to patient care. You’ll communicate directly with veterinarians and nursing teams throughout the hospital.

You can continue growing: Working in a 24/7 emergency and specialty hospital will expose you to complex cases and a wide range of diagnostic testing. You’ll have opportunities to strengthen your skills, share your knowledge, and keep learning.

About VERG Brooklyn

VERG Brooklyn is a leading 24/7 emergency and specialty veterinary hospital serving pets and their families throughout the tri-state area. Our specialists and emergency teams provide care across departments including Emergency and Critical Care, Surgery, Neurology, Internal Medicine, Cardiology, and Oncology.

Here, your laboratory skills will support patients who need everything from routine testing to urgent, lifesaving care.

Benefits That Support You

We appreciate the care and precision our employees bring to VERG Brooklyn every day. Our benefits package includes:

• Competitive compensation

• Flexible scheduling

• Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance

• FSA and HSA options, including company contributions

• Interest-free health and veterinary payment account

• 401(k) with company match

• Paid time off and floating holidays

• Commuter benefits

• Uniform allowance

• Employee pet-care and veterinary service discounts

• Additional employee benefits and perks

What You’ll Do

As a Veterinary Laboratory Technician, you’ll process samples and complete diagnostic testing accurately and efficiently. You’ll help ensure urgent cases are prioritized and results are available when our medical teams need them.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Performing hematology, chemistry, coagulation, urinalysis, cytology, and microbiology testing.

• Preparing, processing, labeling, and storing samples.

• Preparing and staining cytology slides and providing interpretation support.

• Operating and maintaining equipment such as IDEXX and Abaxis analyzers, microscopes, and centrifuges.

• Entering results accurately and promptly into electronic medical records.

• Monitoring quality control standards.

• Troubleshooting equipment and testing issues.

• Communicating with medical teams to prioritize urgent samples.

• Keeping the laboratory clean, organized, and well stocked.

• Helping train new team members when needed.

What You Bring

You have at least two years of experience in a veterinary or medical laboratory setting, including experience in a referral or specialty hospital. You’re comfortable working with common laboratory techniques, veterinary analyzers, and diagnostic equipment.

You’re someone who:

• Takes pride in producing accurate, dependable results.

• Notices the small details without losing sight of urgent priorities.

• Stays organized while managing multiple tests and requests.

• Communicates clearly and works well with others.

• Remains calm and focused when the hospital gets busy.

• Is willing to help, learn, and share knowledge with the team.

Because VERG Brooklyn cares for patients 24 hours a day, seven days a week, scheduling flexibility is important. This position may include evenings, weekends, and holidays. Available schedules will be discussed during the interview process.

What's Next?

If you would like to work for a hospital that gives you the platform to do amazing things, we would love to learn more about you! If you'd like to check us out before applying:

Our website:  https://www.verg-brooklyn.com/
Our FB Page:   https://www.facebook.com/VERGBrooklyn/

$24—$27 USD

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist - Central Operations and Telemetry, Part Time, Variable shifts
jobs.description:
• 20 hours per week
• 8 hour variable shifts rotating days and evenings

The Clinical Pharmacist PNE reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Pharmacist PNE is responsible for identifying, preventing, and/or resolving medication related problems; for providing authoritative  information to other health care professionals, patients, and the public; and for assuring that the informational, clinical, and drug distribution components of pharmacy services function as an integrated system to provide patient centered care to the patients and staff of Northwestern Medicine.

The mission of the Department of Pharmacy is to deliver the safest, highest quality, most effective and efficient patient care while developing the best people, advancing research, and integrating pharmacy services to successfully coordinate care across the Northwestern Medicine enterprise.

The vision of the Department of Pharmacy is to be a recognized as a national leader in advancing the pharmacy enterprise through excellence, innovation, education and research.

Meets the professional exemption under FLSA; but works an irregular schedule.

Responsibilities:

• Interprets medication orders to ensure safety and proper use of medications and is alert to compatibilities, incompatibilities, medication duplication, medication allergies, and potential medication administration errors. Coordinates the solving of medication related problems between pharmacy, nursing, and prescribers, demonstrating initiative and sound judgment.
• Monitors medication therapy for significant drug-drug, drug-diet, or drug-laboratory test interactions. Intervenes in circumstances of significant interactions, therapeutic duplications, and other occasions where pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic expertise is warranted.
• Evaluates and documents that the medication(s) selected are appropriate for achieving the desired therapeutic outcome. Communicates potential problems and likely solutions to the prescriber.
• Acts as a consultant in the areas of pharmacokinetics and adverse reactions to physicians, nurses and other healthcare professionals. Participates in all therapeutic drug monitoring or intervention programs; adjusting therapy as indicated by patient condition and laboratory results.
• Processes all medication order information into the Electronic Health Record to ensure accuracy of records regarding past, current and future dispensing and charging.
• Maintains a comprehensive pharmacy patient profile. The profile should include age, maturation, weight, allergies, diagnosis, estimated and actual pharmacokinetic parameters, and pertinent information which may affect medication therapy decisions.
• Oversees the packaging labeling, and distribution of medications for all patients and employees according to established policies, procedures, and guidelines. Monitors the use of scheduled medications on the nursing units and maintains controlled inventories of medication in the dispensing areas.
• Compounds and dispenses pharmaceuticals including sterile products, chemotherapy and parenteral nutrition products.
• Verifies medication orders before delivery to patient care areas and ensures accuracy and completeness. Resolves discrepancies as necessary.
• Reviews all laboratory data for appropriateness of medication use and recommends changes when needed. Including microbial culture and sensitivity data, toxicology, therapeutic drug monitoring, etc.
• Develops and presents orientation, education and training programs for medical, nursing, hospital and pharmacy staff, as well as assisting in the educating of pharmacy students, residents, and fellows.
• Educates patients and their families about specific medications.
• Responds to emergency situations to assist with medication management (e.g. response to cardiac arrests)
• Provides accurate and timely medication information and or teaching to healthcare professionals or patients.
• Maintains the hospital formulary and acts to limit medication usage to formulary items when appropriate
• Documents all clinical activities and interventions performed. Collects data, maintains logs, records and other documentation as required by the department
• Communicates professional knowledge effectively in both oral and written forms to patients and other health professionals.
• Participates in quality improvement and medication use review activities of the department.
• Organizes, prioritizes, and plans workload within given time constraints. Works cooperatively with fellow pharmacists to oversee and direct the activities of the work area, to assign work to technicians, and to assure that the established department objectives are accomplished
• Reviews restocking automated dispensing cabinets (ADC’s) throughout the hospital and resolves any problems.
• Ensures compliance with hazardous waste collection and disposal procedures.
• Maintains proficiency and expertise in area/s of practice through continuous professional development.
• All other job duties as assigned.

Required

• Active Clinical Pharmacist license in the state of Illinois (IDFPR)
• Bachelor’s Degree in Pharmacy or a Doctor of Pharmacy Degree

Preferred

• Training and knowledge of specialty areas (neonatology, critical care, oncology, etc.)
• Completion of a pharmacy residency program or equivalent hospital pharmacy experience

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

Background Check

Northwestern Medicine conducts a background check that includes criminal history on newly hired team members and, at times, internal transfers. If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used in some portions of the candidate review process for this position, however, all employment decisions will be made by a person.

We offer a wide range of benefits that provide employees with tools and resources to improve their physical, emotional, and financial well-being while providing protection for unexpected life events.

jobs.title: Director, Nonclinical and Translational Science
jobs.description:
Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs. Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. We are a clinical-stage company currently focused on post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), Wolfram syndrome, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Our mission is powered by our people. Our core values – be audacious, be curious, be authentic, be engaged, and be accountable – creating a culture of caring. Amylyx has assembled an experienced team ready to take action because the communities we serve have no time to wait. If you share our passion and are determined to tackle some of medicine’s toughest problems, we encourage you to read the opportunity below and apply.

The Opportunity

The Director, Nonclinical and Translational Science will provide strategic and scientific leadership for nonclinical and translational programs across the development portfolio. This individual will lead programs from candidate nomination through IND-enabling development, regulatory submission, and translation into first-in-human clinical trials and beyond. Working closely with cross-functional R&D teams, the Director will integrate pharmacology, toxicology, biomarker, and clinical insights to define development strategies, identify and mitigate risks, and enable data-driven decisions that advance novel therapeutics for patients.

This person will also:

• Provide strategic and scientific leadership for nonclinical safety and translational science, informing portfolio decisions, development strategy, and regulatory interactions.

• Partner with Pharmacology, Clinical Development, Biomarkers, and other functions to establish integrated plans that connect mechanism, exposure, pharmacodynamic activity, safety, and clinical translation.

• Represent Nonclinical and Translational Science on cross-functional project teams, providing clear recommendations and proactively addressing program risks and evidence gaps.

• Evaluate external assets and technologies for potential in-licensing opportunities in partnership with Business Development and cross-functional subject matter experts.

• Provide expertise in Immunology concepts, application to program design and strategy, and clinical translation and progression.

Responsibilities

• Lead nonclinical and translational studies for assigned programs from candidate nomination through IND-enabling development, regulatory submission.

• Support the clinical teams on first-in-human studies and subsequent clinical development.

• Develop and maintain integrated nonclinical development plans, including pharmacology, toxicology, immunotoxicology, safety pharmacology, toxicokinetics, bioanalytical, immunogenicity, and translational activities aligned with program objectives and regulatory expectations.

• Define translational strategies that connect preclinical findings to clinical hypotheses, including data to support dose and exposure projections, biomarker plans, and evidence needed to support early clinical development.

• Serve as immunology subject matter expert on assigned studies and other pipeline programs across the portfolio.

• Provide scientific subject matter expertise in nonclinical development and immunology with clear recommendations at program governance and portfolio decision points, including assessment of risks, data gaps, timelines, and resource needs.

• Serve as CRO sponsor representative and monitor for outsourced in vivo studies and bioanalytical studies as assigned, and hold accountable CROs, consultants, toxicology laboratories, and other external partners to timelines and study plans; ensure studies are scientifically rigorous, timely, compliant, and fit for purpose.

• Interpret and integrate nonclinical and emerging clinical data to refine program strategy, investigate safety signals, and guide studies that support continued clinical development and registration.

• Lead preparation and review of nonclinical and translational content for regulatory documents, including briefing books, INDs, Investigator’s Brochures, NDAs, BLAs, and MAAs.

• Contribute to evaluation of external opportunities and provide nonclinical and translational due diligence in support of business development activities.

• Mentor and influence colleagues across disciplines, foster rigorous scientific discussion, and help strengthen nonclinical and translational capabilities across the organization.

Required Qualifications

• PhD or equivalent degree in Toxicology, Pharmacology, or a related scientific discipline with 9+ years of relevant post degree pharmaceutical or biotechnology experience; or a Master’s degree with 12+ years of relevant experience post degree.

• Demonstrated leadership of nonclinical development programs from candidate nomination through IND-enabling studies, IND submission, and first-in-human clinical development.

• Subject matter expertise in immunology, supported by hands industry experience and/or immunology degree.

• Broad expertise in pharmaceutical toxicology and working knowledge of discovery toxicology, safety pharmacology, toxicokinetics, bioanalysis, pathology, and relevant regulatory guidelines.

• Experience integrating nonclinical pharmacology, safety, exposure, biomarker, and clinical data to support dose selection, clinical monitoring, and development decisions.

• Experience authoring and reviewing nonclinical sections of regulatory submissions; IND experience is required, and experience with NDAs, BLAs, or MAAs is desirable.

• Demonstrated ability to select, manage, and oversee CROs and external experts, including study design, monitoring, data review, and issue resolution.

• Strong cross-functional leadership, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to translate complex science into clear recommendations for technical and senior-leadership audiences.

• Ability to prioritize, make sound decisions under uncertainty, and solve problems effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

• Ability to travel domestically up to 10–15%.

Work Location and Conditions

• At Amylyx, we proudly support remote work opportunities within the United States. However, due to business considerations related to health insurance coverage and state tax regulations, we are unable to hire employees who reside and/or work in certain states. Currently, we are not considering applicants from Alaska and Hawaii.

• You will be expected to travel to our corporate location in Cambridge, MA several times a year and attend other company-related events as necessary and requested.

• You must have access to work in setting which enables meeting all requirements of the role (including privacy, reliable internet access, phone, ability to video conference, etc.) at your remote location.

Compensation

The pay range posted below represents our good faith estimate of compensation for this role, based on market data and internal benchmarks. The final offer may vary depending on a candidate’s experience, skills, and qualifications, as well as considerations of internal equity.

Estimated Pay Range

$216,000—$243,000 USD

To stay connected with us, follow Amylyx Pharmaceuticals on LinkedIn.

To return to our website please click here.

Amylyx Pharmaceuticals is an Equal Opportunity Employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race, color, creed, religion, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, age, sex or gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, pregnancy-related conditions, and lactation), gender identity or expression (including transgender status), sexual orientation, marital status, military service and veteran status, physical or mental disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws and ordinances. Amylyx’s management team is dedicated to this policy with respect to recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, employee activities, access to facilities and programs, and general treatment during employment. Accommodations are available for candidates who require them in our selection process. If you need an accommodation, please let your Amylyx Talent Acquisition contact know.

jobs.title: Network Engineer, Connectivity
jobs.description:
Simplesense builds, deploys, and sustains the Installation Resilience Platform that enables mission operators to rapidly adapt and respond. The Platform protects critical infrastructure from cyber attack while unlocking previously siloed information to monitor, diagnose, and improve response times to incidents. Our adversaries rapidly adopt the latest technology: we help defense users respond in kind.

Simplesense is a non-traditional defense contractor and prime on the Air Force's Installation Resilience Operations Command and Control (IROC) program, which is now expanding to five additional Air Force, Space Force, and Army installations from the one prototype installation, Tyndall Air Force Base.

Our team combines over 100 years of direct mission experience solving hard problems with 50 years technical expertise deploying DevSecOps, cybersecurity, and cloud infrastructure, giving us a deep appreciation for our customers’ mission and end users’ priorities. We build for scale, architecting and prioritizing technical work for long term sustainability.

Network Engineer, Connectivity

Location: We prioritize candidates who reside in the Denver, CO area (hybrid as needed) but we are open to exceptional remote talent.

Department: Engineering

About Simplesense

Simplesense keeps military installations mission-ready. The infrastructure their operations depend on — power, water, fuel, facilities, security, and communications — runs continuously, often under strain. When it fails without warning, mission readiness is at risk, and the people who run these installations need to see what’s happening in time to act. That’s the foundation of Continuous Mission Assurance.

We securely integrate Operational Technology and Control Systems (OT/CS) from the building edge to the cloud, applying Zero Trust principles to protect critical infrastructure from cyber and physical threats. By unlocking previously siloed data, we put timely awareness in front of the decision-makers who need it. As prime on the Air Force’s Installation Resilience Operations Command and Control (IROC) program, we hold a continuous Authority to Operate (ATO) and have proven the capability at scale at Tyndall Air Force Base. That work is now expanding across the Air Force, Space Force, and Army.

Our team pairs over a century of boots-on-the-ground mission experience with deep technical expertise across DevSecOps, cybersecurity, and cloud infrastructure. We engineer resilient infrastructure — the software, integration, and operational backbone behind it — for the operators who depend on it in the field. Persistent resilience, built for the mission.

About the Role

As our Network Engineer, Connectivity, you will play an important role in deploying, operating, and maintaining the secure network infrastructure that connects customer facilities to our hybrid-cloud platform services. You will implement and validate network solutions across enterprise, facility, OT/ICS, and hybrid-cloud environments, helping ensure our networks remain resilient, secure, and supportable.

You will work hands-on across the lifecycle of Connectivity infrastructure, including customer facility onboarding, network configuration, production operations, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management. You will partner closely with the Connectivity, broader engineering, and customer technical teams to reliably deliver network services, resolve operational challenges, and continuously improve our networking capabilities.

Work Model: We prioritize candidates who reside in the Denver, CO area (hybrid as needed) but we are open to exceptional remote talent.

• Locals: Onsite as needed for collaborative workspace time.

• Remote: Quarterly travel to hub locations for team syncs and alignment.

Our Performance Culture

We measure performance across two key dimensions: How you perform your role (Our Core Values) and What your role entails (Your Execution).

How You’ll Work — Our Core Values

At Simplesense, we value high-trust autonomy. We look for builders who can comfortably navigate ambiguity and are deeply driven by our shared national security mission.

• People Always – Win as One Team: We foster a culture of psychological safety and mutual support. We operate as an integrated team where we assume noble intent as our default setting, ensuring that even the toughest feedback is rooted in trust. We trade our silos for a shared mission because collective impact always outweighs individual achievement.

• Empathize – Obsess Over the Customer: We don't just solve technical problems; we empathize and advocate for the operators using our products. We look beyond the surface to build what our customers—both internal and external—actually need to succeed, not just what they asked for.

• Focus – Ruthlessly Prioritize with Urgency: We focus on the highest-impact work and ruthlessly say no to distractions. We build resilient systems so that our solutions can repeat and scale under pressure.

• Let’s Go – Catalyze the Change You Seek: We don't wait for the industry to change; we drive it. We seek to understand why things are the way they are, but we never use “the way it’s always been” as an excuse. We aren't afraid to change course when the data or our mission demands it.

What You’ll Do

• Network Design & Implementation: Implement, configure, and validate secure network solutions using established architectures and standards across routing, switching, segmentation, VLANs/VRFs, firewalls, VPNs, high availability, addressing, and facility-to-cloud connectivity. Identify design risks and recommend improvements.

• Customer Network Design & Onboarding: Translate approved customer network designs and implementation plans into working configurations. Execute networking activities across factory preparation, facility installation, testing, validation, acceptance, and operational handoff.

• Network Reliability & Incident Response: Monitor and maintain the health, availability, and performance of assigned network services and customer environments. Investigate escalated production issues, perform network diagnostics, safely restore services using established procedures, and contribute to reliability improvements.

• Security by Design: Implement and maintain network segmentation, firewall policies, access controls, encrypted connectivity, and secure management configurations that align with established security standards and protect customer operational environments.

• Network Automation & Configuration Engineering: Contribute to reusable configuration templates, automated validation, configuration compliance, diagnostics, and deployment workflows that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and minimize configuration drift across customer environments.

• Lifecycle & Change Management: Execute planned network changes, upgrades, patching, vulnerability remediation, failover testing, hardware replacement, and infrastructure lifecycle activities using established change management, validation, and rollback procedures.

• Engineering Standards & Collaboration: Maintain accurate network diagrams, configurations, implementation records, troubleshooting guidance, and operational documentation. Collaborate with senior engineers on technical designs and complex problems, contribute to engineering reviews, and continuously strengthen the team's network engineering practices.

What You Bring

Required Qualifications:

• Experience: 5+ years of hands-on network engineering experience configuring, deploying, troubleshooting, and supporting production network environments.

• Network Engineering Knowledge: Solid understanding of TCP/IP and Layer-2/Layer-3 networking, including routing and switching, VLANs, subnetting, NAT, network redundancy, and familiarity with dynamic routing protocols such as BGP and OSPF. CompTIA Network+ / Security+ certification or the ability to achieve certification within the first 90 days of employment.

• Network Security: Hands-on experience configuring and troubleshooting firewalls, ACLs, network segmentation, site-to-site VPNs, and secure network access within established security architectures.

• Network Operations & Troubleshooting: Experience diagnosing network connectivity, availability, and performance issues using packet captures, routing and switching information, device logs, monitoring systems, and network diagnostic tools.

• Automation & Configuration Management: Familiarity with scripting, configuration templates, version control, or network automation tools used to improve network provisioning, configuration consistency, validation, and operational workflows.

• Technical Execution & Collaboration: Demonstrated ability to independently execute defined technical work, troubleshoot and resolve operational problems, identify risks and escalation needs, communicate technical findings clearly, and collaborate effectively with other engineers and technical teams.

• Travel: Ability to travel for customer facility deployments and team collaboration.

• Compliance: Must be a U.S. Citizen and capable of obtaining a DoD NIPR network account and Common Access Card (CAC).

• Security Clearance: Must have, or be able to obtain, a DoD Secret Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Prior experience working within DoD, Air Force, Space Force, or fast-paced Federal contractor/dual-use startup environments.

• Relevant technical certifications such as CCNA or equivalent demonstrated expertise.

• Experience with OT/ICS, critical infrastructure, industrial networks, facility-edge environments, or network architectures requiring IT/OT segmentation and controlled connectivity.

• Familiarity with critical-infrastructure security practices and frameworks such as NIST guidance, ISA/IEC 62443, MITRE ATT&CK for ICS, or comparable standards.

• Experience with network automation and configuration-management technologies such as Python, Ansible, configuration templates, or network source-of-truth systems.

• Experience with Linux networking, cloud networking, and hybrid on-premises/cloud connectivity.

What Success Looks Like (First 90 Days)

• 30 Days: Ramp up on Connectivity network architectures, customer environments, configuration standards, monitoring systems, lab environments, facility-onboarding workflows, and the production support model. Build working relationships across Connectivity, Engineering, Security, User Success, and adjacent teams.

• 60 Days: Independently execute well-defined network configuration, validation, maintenance, and troubleshooting tasks. Contribute to active customer onboarding or production operations, identify opportunities to improve documentation, monitoring, configuration consistency, or automation, and demonstrate sound technical judgment when escalating complex issues.

• 90 Days: Reliably own assigned network operations, configuration, or facility-onboarding activities within established architectures and procedures. Deliver a practical improvement that increases network reliability, security, repeatability, or supportability, and demonstrate growing independence in troubleshooting, technical planning, and operational execution.

Compensation and Benefits

Pay Range: $103k-$139k per year. Compensation is determined based on experience, skill level, and location. We review ranges regularly to ensure market competitiveness.

Competitive Benefits

• Equity

• Medical, Life, Short-Term Disability, and AD&D insurance

• Medical travel coverage

• Dental coverage

• Vision coverage

• 401k matching

Our Typical Hiring Process

• Find Your Fit: Your journey starts here. Explore and apply to our open positions to find the right role for your skills.

• Initial Chat: A brief call with our recruiting team to learn about your background and answer your initial questions about Simplesense.

• Values & Vision: A conversation with a hiring manager to discuss how your aspirations align with our mission and goals of the team.

• Show Your Skills: Complete a technical assessment that reflects the work you’d be doing.

• Team Interview: Interview with the team to discuss your experience and see if we’re a great match.

• Final Handshake: A final conversation to ensure we’ve answered all your questions before making a decision.

• Welcome to Simplesense!

Simplesense is an equal opportunity employer committed to a policy of merit-based employment. All employment decisions—including recruitment, hiring, promotion, compensation, benefits, training, and termination—are made based on individual qualifications, performance, and business needs. We strictly prohibit discrimination or harassment of any kind on the basis of protected characteristics as recognized by federal, state, or local law. As a U.S. government contractor, Simplesense complies with all applicable equal employment opportunity laws, Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act, and the Vietnam Era Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act (VEVRAA). If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete the application or take part in the interview process, please contact People Operations at careers@simplesense.io.

jobs.title: Head of Demand Generation
jobs.description:
ABOUT WARP

Warp is the AI-native Employee Management Platform for ambitious companies. HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, tax compliance, and more, all built from scratch on one AI-native platform.

Every company runs on its people, and the software that manages them is some of the oldest in the enterprise. Incumbents like ADP and Workday built their businesses on complexity and large ops teams. Warp is built for AI to be the primary operator. Every advance in LLM capability widens our lead.

We process $X billion in annual payments for high-growth companies across all 50 US states + globally.

We've raised $85M from Battery Ventures, Sapphire Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures (Ashton Kutcher), and Y Combinator, alongside operators including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Claire Hughes Johnson (Stripe), and the founders of Dropbox and Replit. Our team comes from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Gusto, Rippling, and more.

We hire people who ship constantly, own outcomes, and care about craft. If you want to automate an entire category of work that every company depends on, this is the place.

About the Role

We're hiring a Head of Demand Generation to own the top of Warp's funnel and turn our Series B momentum into pipeline. You'll own how ambitious companies discover Warp and decide to talk to us: paid, SEO, content, email, lifecycle, web conversion, and the demand programs that feed a growing sales team. You'll partner closely with our COO on brand and with our Head of Sales on conversion.

This is a builder and player-coach role. You'll set the strategy, write the content, run channels, dig into the data, and build the demand gen function as Warp scales.



What You'll Do

 - Own marketing-sourced pipeline as a number, driving 3–4x coverage on the bookings target.

 - Own inbound demand gen strategy and execution across all channels

 - Build and run integrated campaigns across content, email, paid, SEO, and organic that generate qualified pipeline.

 - Own the website and conversion funnel, from messaging and landing pages to CRO and experimentation.

 - Manage paid advertising across Google, LinkedIn, and other channels

 - Write content and campaign messaging that speaks directly to People, Ops, and Finance leaders.

 - Partner closely with the sales team to align campaigns with pipeline goals, attribution, routing and conversion

 - Build reporting to understand performance, optimize spend, and make smart investment decisions.

 - Build and lead the demand gen function as Warp scales.



What We're Looking For

 - 6+ years in demand gen or growth marketing at a B2B sales-led SaaS company

 - Proven track record building inbound programs that generate measurable pipeline

 - Strong writer who can create compelling content and campaign messaging for a business audience.

 - Hands-on experience across paid, SEO, email, and lifecycle marketing.

 - Data-driven and analytical - you think in funnels and can tie spend to pipeline to revenue.

 - Player-coach who can run channels yourself today and build a team as we grow.

 - Strong partnership with Sales and a revenue-first mindset.



Nice to Have

 - Experience marketing to founders, finance, or people and ops buyers.

 - Fintech, HR tech, or developer-adjacent background.

 - Prior experience managing a small team



Success Metrics

You'll be measured on:

 - Inbound MQL volume and quality

 - Pipeline sourced and influenced by marketing

 - Website traffic and conversion rates

 - SEO rankings and organic search growth

 - Paid CAC and ROAS across channels


BENEFITS AT WARP: 

 - 100% Health Coverage: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your dependents.

 - 401(k) Matching: Start investing in your future from day one.

 - Flexible PTO: We offer uncapped flexible PTO, meaning you’re trusted to take the time you need to recharge while balancing your responsibilities and team commitments.

 - Commuter Benefits: Pre-tax commuter benefits for your daily trip to our NYC office.

 - Catered Lunch Daily: Great food, every day, on us. No meal prep, no decision fatigue.

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
ABOUT WARP

Warp is the AI-native Employee Management Platform for ambitious companies. HRIS, payroll, benefits, IT, tax compliance, and more, all built from scratch on one AI-native platform.

Every company runs on its people, and the software that manages them is some of the oldest in the enterprise. Incumbents like ADP and Workday built their businesses on complexity and large ops teams. Warp is built for AI to be the primary operator. Every advance in LLM capability widens our lead.

We process $X billion in annual payments for high-growth companies across all 50 US states + globally.

We've raised $85M from Battery Ventures, Sapphire Ventures, Peak XV, Sound Ventures (Ashton Kutcher), and Y Combinator, alongside operators including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Claire Hughes Johnson (Stripe), and the founders of Dropbox and Replit. Our team comes from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Gusto, Rippling, and more.

We hire people who ship constantly, own outcomes, and care about craft. If you want to automate an entire category of work that every company depends on, this is the place.


ABOUT THE ROLE 

We're hiring a Head of Finance to build and own the financial engine of a company scaling revenue to $50M+. You'll be the CEO's primary partner on strategic finance: the operating model, board and investor reporting, unit economics, and the capital decisions that come with an $85M-raised, money-moving business. You'll start hands-on and build the team beneath you over time.



What you'll do

 - Own the financial model and forecast. Turn the charter's revenue trajectory into a plan the company runs against and a model the board trusts.

 - Run board and investor reporting: monthly metrics, quarterly board materials, and the financial narrative behind both.

 - Own unit economics and pricing analysis. ARPU, gross margin, payback, and the economics of new lines like benefits brokerage and in-house payroll rails.

 - Partner on capital allocation. Where the Series B goes, how we think about burn and runway, and the return on big bets like replacing our money-movement vendor.

 - Build the finance function. Hire and lead the controller and ops side, and own relationships with our wealth, banking, and accounting partners and our auditors.

 - Be the financial backbone of the next fundraise when it comes.



What we're looking for:

 - 5+ years in finance, including ownership of FP&A and board reporting at a high-growth startup.

 - Deep FP&A and strategic finance ability. You can build a model yourself from scratch and defend all assumptions to a board.

 - You are fluent in SaaS metrics, and ideally fintech or payments economics: float, money movement, and multi-product ARPU.

 - You've partnered directly with a founder or CEO to make decisions and build.

 - You can be hands-on now, and a team-builder later. No task is beneath our leadership at this stage.



Nice to Have:

 - Experience in the payroll, payments, insurance space, or another regulated money-moving business.

 - You've helped run a priced fundraise.


BENEFITS AT WARP: 

 - 100% Health Coverage: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your dependents.

 - 401(k) Matching: Start investing in your future from day one.

 - Flexible PTO: We offer uncapped flexible PTO, meaning you’re trusted to take the time you need to recharge while balancing your responsibilities and team commitments.

 - Commuter Benefits: Pre-tax commuter benefits for your daily trip to our NYC office.

 - Catered Lunch Daily: Great food, every day, on us. No meal prep, no decision fatigue.

 - Quarterly Offsites: Beautiful locations to connect as a team. Past locations include Spain, Catskills, and San Francisco.

Warp is based in New York City, and most of our team works together in-office 5x per week. Please refer to the top of this page for this position's hiring location and working model.

The Clinical Practice Specialist reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Clinical Practice Specialist leads efforts to ensure quality clinical practice and professional development at the front-line.

Responsibilities:

Quality:

• Supports staff to seek/maintain specialty certification including monitoring progress and completion.
• Participates in review of unit/division dashboard through LDOC and assesses for opportunities to improve in quality and practice areas; develops corresponding action as needed with key unit/division stakeholders.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT FINCH

Our mission is to make justice radically more accessible to every American household.

We combine expert operators with purpose-built AI to automate the admin work of consumer law and put clients first by handling intake, claim opening, medical records, police reports, lien management, demands, and everything in between.

Since launching in April 2025, we’ve raised a $20M Series A https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-finch-ai-powered-justice backed by Sequoia, Redpoint, and the founders & CEOs of DoorDash, Ironclad, and Digits and are running pre-litigation for over 125 of the highest-volume personal injury firms https://www.finchlegal.com/customers across the country.

Explore life at Finch https://app.notion.com/p/Life-at-Finch-32fe7a322002810cabf6f9547800f2a2?pvs=21 for more.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Finch’s product serves three groups, and each one has to succeed for us to keep growing:

 - Operators: our case managers, who work alongside AI agents on every case. They need agents to handle more on their own, a fast way to verify that work, and a clear next action on every file.

 - Law firms: attorneys who hand us their cases. They need to trust our work, see where every case stands without asking, and get clear guidance on what would make their firm more successful.

 - Clients: injured people counting on their case moving forward. They need to know where things stand and what’s needed from them.

This role owns the operator experience, which sits at the center of the other two. It comes down to three questions:

 - What can agents do on their own? Decide which work agents complete without human input, where they need sign-off, and how that line moves as they earn trust.

 - How do we verify their work quickly? Design how operators check what agents have done, catch what’s wrong, and move forward without redoing it.

 - What happens next? When a case manager opens a file, make it obvious what’s been done, what needs them, and what to do next.

You’ll report to Ben, our co-founder and CTO. You’ll spend real time with operators, set the direction and priorities, ship with our engineers, and measure success by operator speed, work quality, and how much agents handle on their own.




WHAT WILL MAKE YOU SUCCESSFUL


YOU’LL LIKELY THRIVE IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience owning meaningful product work in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment, from discovery through execution and iteration.

 - A track record of deeply understanding user journeys, operational workflows, and the decisions people need to make within them.

 - Strong product judgment: you can turn complex workflows into clear experiences, priorities, and practical next steps.

 - The ability to reason through how people and AI agents work together, making agent activity, suggested actions, escalations, and human responsibilities understandable.

 - The ability to earn trust with engineers and cross-functional partners, align them around a product direction, and follow through on delivery.

 - A habit of staying close to users after launch and judging success by whether they can understand what happened, take the right next action, and complete work efficiently and well.


IT’S A PLUS IF YOU HAVE

 - Experience building AI-powered products or workflows that combine automation with human decisions and handoffs.

 - Experience with workflow-heavy, operational, or B2B products.

 - Experience building products for users working in high-trust or high-stakes environments.

 - Experience helping establish product practices at an early-stage or rapidly changing company.


THIS ROLE MAY NOT BE FOR YOU IF

 - You prefer a role where the roadmap, process, and success metrics are already defined.

 - You are looking for a narrow remit rather than ownership from user discovery through delivery and iteration.

 - You need a fixed organizational structure and fully defined product-area ownership before you can do your best work.




WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

We aim to run a human, efficient process. That generally includes:

 1. Intro: An initial conversation about your background, motivation, and the role.

 2. Interview: A deeper dive with a leader on the team.

 3. Case Interview: A practical exercise that gives you a sense of the problems we’re solving and of how you approach a product problem, make tradeoffs, and turn your thinking into a clear direction.

 4. Onsite: A chance to meet the team and explore the work together.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Integrated Campaigns & Field Marketing
jobs.description:
About Tekmetric

Tekmetric is the all-in-one, cloud-based software helping auto repair shops run smarter, grow faster, and serve customers better.

Built by a shop owner and shaped by the needs of the industry, Tekmetric brings together innovation, real-world experience, and a thriving community to help shops thrive - not just survive. From running a shop, to securing payments to engaging customers, our platform simplifies operations so shop owners can focus on what really matters: delivering exceptional service, earning trust, and growing sustainably.

Officially founded in Houston in 2017, Tekmetric has grown from a single shop’s vision to the industry’s leading solution - all by staying true to our values of transparency, integrity, innovation, and a service-first mindset.

But we’re not just building shop management software. We’re building a movement. We’re empowering repair shops to rise above the daily grind, create meaningful connections with their customers, and lead the industry forward - one interaction at a time.

Come build with us. Join the journey. Shape the future of auto repair.

Working the Tekmetric Way

At Tekmetric, we’re building a culture where winning matters - not for ego, but because when our customers win, we win together.

We move fast, stay curious, and take full ownership of our results — no excuses, no finger-pointing. If you thrive in ambiguity, take initiative, and view honest feedback as fuel for growth, you’ll feel right at home here.

We’re direct but respectful, ambitious yet grounded, and collaborative at every level. Everyone leads through impact and is encouraged to speak up, share ideas, and challenge assumptions (even your manager’s). This is a place for builders, not bystanders.

Success here takes focus, follow-through, and a willingness to roll up your sleeves — but if you’re driven by meaningful work and real results, it’s deeply rewarding. You’ll join a team that cares about the work, supports one another, and takes smart risks to achieve bold goals. Be yourself, stay mission-focused, and you’ll thrive. If that energizes you, we can’t wait to meet you.

Where We Work: At Tekmetric, great work happens anywhere, but great teams are built through intentional connection. We offer hybrid and remote work models based on your proximity to our office hubs. Because we value in-person collaboration, travel is an expected part of every role. We come together several times a year for team and company-wide offsites to align on goals and strengthen relationships. Attendance at these events is expected and fully supported.

Tekmetric is seeking a Senior Director, Integrated Marketing to own how we reach the shops our digital engine can't reach alone. Our inbound engine captures shops that are already looking for a solution. This role builds the complementary motion: coordinated campaigns, partner channels, and in-field presence that put Tekmetric in front of the rest of our 250,000-shop addressable market, in the places where shop owners actually learn, gather, and make decisions.

You'll own three connected programs: integrated campaign planning, partner marketing, and field marketing. Together they turn our brand and product story into pipeline, expand awareness and trust across SMB and Mid-Market segments, and open channels that scale access to the market beyond what paid and organic search can deliver.

You're a builder and a connector. You plan with the precision of a strategist, execute with the urgency of an operator, and are ready to be held accountable for the pipeline and market coverage your programs create.

What You'll Do

• Own the integrated campaign strategy and planning calendar across SMB and mid-market segments, with clear pipeline targets for each.

• Lead multi-channel campaign activation, including ABM, nurture programs, and launch campaigns with Product Marketing.

• Direct field marketing in partnership with regional sales leaders, so that marketing supports each territory's goals.

• Direct partner marketing, so that co-marketing and partner programs produce measurable pipeline and adoption.

• Work with Digital Growth on one shared acquisition target, so channel execution and campaign planning are aligned.

• Work with Sales leadership on lead quality, handoffs, follow-up, and feedback loops.

• Work with Events and Customer Marketing so that national events, regional programs, and customer advocacy support campaigns.

• Build the team's operating rhythm: planning, reviews, reporting, and clear ownership of each program.

• Hire, coach, and develop team members, and set clear goals and standards of quality.

• Report on pipeline and program performance to leadership, including what to start, stop, and change.

What You'll Bring

• 10–12+ years in integrated marketing, field marketing, partner marketing, or demand generation roles in SaaS or high-growth tech, with meaningful time at the Director level or above

• Proven track record owning integrated campaign planning across multiple segments (SMB, Mid-Market, and/or Enterprise) and driving measurable pipeline and revenue outcomes

• Experience leading a mix of functions, such as campaigns, ABM, field, and partner marketing.

• Demonstrated experience building field marketing programs, including co-hosted partner events, field events, and full territory plans developed with Sales, with clear ROI and a track record of working alongside a dedicated events team

• Experience marketing to fragmented, distributed SMB audiences at scale, specifically reaching a buyer who doesn't behave like a typical enterprise buyer (no big procurement cycles, short attention spans, word-of-mouth driven)

• Strong analytical and planning instincts: you build the model, own the number, and explain the delta, including attribution for influenced as well as sourced pipeline

• Ability to build strong, trust-based partnerships with Sales, Business Development, RevOps, Finance, and Product, and to work effectively with external partners and sponsors

• Experience building and developing a team: hiring, structuring, and elevating the people around you

• Comfort operating at a senior level: executive-facing communication, high-stakes decisions under uncertainty, and the ability to prioritize ruthlessly in a scaling environment

• Fluency with AI-powered tools and modern martech to increase program velocity, personalization, and measurement without adding headcount

• Willingness to travel regularly to events, partner meetings, and customer locations

• A plus: experience in the automotive aftermarket, field service software, or vertical SaaS for trade-based industries

Why You'll Love Working With Us

Health & Wellness That Have You Covered:

• Enjoy the flexibility of remote work

• Competitive base salaries that reflect your value.

• Flexible PTO — No set number of days, just the trust to take the time you need. We genuinely encourage our team to disconnect and recharge.

• Support for every stage of life—with paid maternity, parental bonding, and medical leave for you or your loved ones.

• Comprehensive health benefits, including Medical, Dental, Vision, and Prescription coverage. For employee only, we offer plans that cover 100% of premiums and we cover 50% of costs for families.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SOURCING MANAGER, ELECTRONICS (STARLINK)

SpaceX is leveraging our experience building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s largest satellite constellation and most advanced broadband internet system. We provide reliable and fast internet to millions of users worldwide, including populations with little or no connectivity, rural communities, aircraft, watercraft, and places where existing services are unreliable, too expensive, or disconnected by natural disasters. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, thousands of satellites and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. The Starlink team is seeking out the best-in-class professionals to maximize Starlink’s potential for communities and businesses around the globe.

As a member of the Starlink Supply Chain team you will manage the sourcing for electronics used on our Starlink Product kits that are shipped to customers. Our team moves quickly and you must too. SpaceX has the unique ability and desire to influence and shape suppliers to be better with us as we challenge our supply chain on cost, quality, and speed of execution.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Develop and manage supply base (domestic and international) for Electronic Components required across our Starlink Product kits

• Work directly with key suppliers to develop and implement sourcing and cost management strategies that support existing platforms and new product development

• Evaluate demand while placing and managing purchase orders according to demand signals

• Track delivery and supplier delivery performance

• Monitor global industry trends, track technology roadmaps, and actively partner with the design teams to identify and mitigate supply and demand challenges

• Partner with internal resources to drive adoption of low-cost parts and avoidance of obsolescence

• Conduct comprehensive supplier analysis, including strategic direction, capacity, market and industry position, and risk assessment

• Manage costs to ensure alignment with program budget

• Present value propositions to executives, including those related to contract award, cost reviews, cost reduction strategies, and critical supply issues

• Work with supply chain engineers to develop requirements for both NPI and production phases

• Negotiate contracts to ensure continuity of supply and protect SpaceX interests

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 9+ years of experience working in one or more of the following:

• Engineering

• Purchasing

• Contract negotiation

• Material or production planning

• Operations or supply chain management

• Material cost control

• Master production scheduling

• Technical procurement or planning experience with raw material commodities

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 6+ years of procurement experience in direct commodity sourcing

• Technical procurement or planning experience with Electronic Components, PCBs, or PCBAs

• Experience in new product introduction (NPI) and mass production (MP)

• Experience reading technical drawings, data sheets, fabrication drawing, BOMs and all related files

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

jobs.title: Applications Engineers, Agentic Workflows
jobs.description:
ABOUT RESCALE

Rescale is pioneering the future of engineering and scientific discovery. As the leader in digital engineering, we’re transforming how products are developed—through intelligent automation, applied AI, data management, and the integration of the world’s largest network of engineering and R&D applications. Joining Rescale means becoming part of a diverse, collaborative, and mission-driven team that’s unlocking faster innovation across industries like aerospace, energy, life sciences, and manufacturing. We’re solving complex challenges that traditional HPC can’t—and we’re seeking passionate, curious minds to help build the next wave of breakthroughs

We are seeking a highly motivated Application Engineer, Agentic Workflows to help build and deliver the next generation of AI Physics capabilities at Rescale!

You will work directly with platform and AI teams to design and ship agent-based capabilities that operate on real engineering tools and data. You will also work closely with customers to apply these agents to real workflows, ensuring what gets built is reliable, repeatable, and productizable.

The role is customer-facing, but product-first. Work done in customer environments must translate into reusable product capabilities rather than one-off solutions.

This role is ideal for engineers who enjoy building real systems, integrating with complex engineering software, and turning early agent prototypes into durable platform capabilities.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and ship agent-driven automation across engineering and CAE workflows

 - Design and implement agents that interact with engineering tools, simulation data, and workflows

 - Encode engineering workflows as structured, agent-executable steps with clear inputs, outputs, and guardrails

 - Integrate agents into end-to-end pipelines as reusable capabilities rather than one-off scripts

 - Harden early agent use cases into deterministic, production-ready systems

 - Debug and resolve issues across agent logic, tool execution, data handling, and orchestration

 - Work directly with customer engineers to understand real workflows and technical constraints

 - Close gaps between real workflows and platform capabilities, feeding concrete learnings back into product direction

 - Operate as a builder first, with the ability to be forward-deployed on critical engagements when needed


CORE SKILL SET

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals, with heavy emphasis on Python

 - Hands-on experience building automation around engineering or technical software

 - Familiarity with CAE workflows, simulation data, and solver-driven processes

 - Experience building or deploying agent-based or LLM-driven systems

 - Experience orchestrating tools, scripts, or workflows across multiple systems

 - Ability to design deterministic, reliable automation around complex tools

 - Experience turning internal automation into reusable, product-grade components

 - Comfortable debugging across tool execution, data handling, and orchestration layers


CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT & TRAVEL

This role includes direct customer engagement during agent deployments and early workflow rollouts. Expect occasional travel to customer sites for deep technical working sessions or critical milestones. Travel is execution-focused and tied to building and deploying real capabilities.




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

AI Agent Applications Engineers ensure that agent-based automation is not just experimental, but reliable, usable, and embedded into real engineering workflows.

Your work will directly influence how engineering organizations adopt agent-driven automation, and will shape the core capabilities that become part of the platform.

Working alongside Geo Partner Managers, the GPM ensures all geo-based teams are aligned and actively driving the joint geo strategy forward.
