jobs.title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) -Online Faculty (part-time)
jobs.description:
Chamberlain University College of Nursing is seeking Online Faculty (part-time) for our Master of Science in Nursing Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (MSN PMHNP) Program. We build long-term relationships with superior educators who are experts in their field and committed to providing the finest in practitioner-focused education.

We are presently accepting applications to meet future need from qualified candidates with interest in teaching a variety of courses.

Courses of instruction include but are not limited to:

NR547 - Differential Diagnosis in Psychiatric-Mental Health Across the Lifespan Practicum - This course will provide students with the fundamental knowledge needed to formulate a differential diagnosis of individuals within the with psychiatric mental health setting. The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders will be introduced, providing the foundation for critical diagnostic skills to cultivate evidence-based behaviors. An emphasis will be placed on processing client information in a logical, progressive manner and formulating differential diagnoses for individuals across the lifespan. The course will include 125 hours of supervised clinical practicum.

NR548 - Psychiatric Assessment for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner - This course expands the knowledge and skills of health assessment principles to perform a thorough psychiatric mental health assessment. The Standards of Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing Practice Advanced Practice Competencies will be introduced. The psychiatric interview will be explored, including interview techniques. Students will develop assessment techniques related to psychiatric history and the review of systems for mental health clients across the lifespan.

NR605 - Diagnosis & Management in Psychiatric-Mental Health across the Lifespan I Practicum - This course will incorporate psychosocial theories and psychotherapy modalities within mental health. Individual and group therapies will be explored as a foundation for non-pharmacological and adjunct treatment of psychiatric mental health disorders across the lifespan. The therapeutic alliance and use of self will be examined. Students will further develop their skills related to health promotion, prevention of illness, diagnosis, and management of acute and chronic mental health problems. Care strategies will include psychotherapy, psychopharmacological prescribing, patient education, follow-up, and referral through a practicum experience in a precepted psychiatric mental health setting.

NR606 - Diagnosis & Management in Psychiatric-Mental Health II Practicum - In this course the student expands knowledge in the care of patients specific to the role of the PMHNP, with a focus on perinatal, child and adolescent populations. Students will further develop their skills related to health promotion, prevention of illness, diagnosis, and management of acute and chronic mental health problems. Care strategies will include psychopharmacological prescribing, psychotherapy, patient education, follow-up, and referral through a practicum experience in a precepted psychiatric mental health setting.

NR607 - Diagnosis & Management in Psychiatric-Mental Health III Practicum - In this course the student will expand upon previous knowledge to include complex mental health diagnoses and psychiatric emergencies. Students will further develop their skills related to health promotion, prevention of illness, diagnosis, and management of complex psychiatric mental health problems across the lifespan. Care strategies will include psychopharmacological prescribing, psychotherapy, patient education, follow-up, and referral through a practicum experience in a precepted psychiatric mental health care setting.

NR668 - Psychiatric-Mental Health Capstone Practicum & Intensive - The student will synthesize all elements of clinical management skills and knowledge and continue to analyze, apply, and evaluate diverse aspects of patient assessment and healthcare intervention. This precepted clinical practicum will be with an approved provider in psychiatric mental health setting. Focus topics include clinical management skills, case studies, chart reviews, and practice critique, with a capstone product evidencing increasing complex psychiatric mental health clinical management skills. At the end of this course the student will be prepared for entry into clinical practice providing psychiatric mental healthcare across the lifespan after first passing the national certification for the psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner.

If you are passionate about nursing and advancing your career through the power of education, we invite you to step forward and apply today!

In this role, you will:

• Inspire students to complete their programs by providing regular, meaningful feedback about their academic performance, development and participation while encouraging them to engage fully in their education.
• Engage students in meaningful asynchronous threaded discussions at least 4 days per week, moderating participation, evaluating responses and rationales, and responding to questions or comments.
• Evaluate academic progress and comprehension of course content through assigning and grading quizzes, exams and writing assignments.
• Exhibit Chamberlain Care ™ by displaying behaviors of care, respect and professionalism, creating a culture that fosters collaboration, cooperation and respect among all.
• Be readily available to meet the needs of a student body that is diverse in age, culture and academic preparation.
• Identify and embrace opportunities to enhance student engagement by reaching out to students in need and responding quickly to requests for help.
• Bring your professional experience to life through professional development, introducing industry perspective into courses and sharing information about nursing trends and opportunities with students.
• Promote student success by demonstrating flexibility in style, schedule, and exhibiting your passion for teaching by devoting time and energy to improve scholarly excellence and subject matter expertise.
• Foster a positive learning environment by maintaining accurate records, submitting grades on time, and enforcing academic policies.
• Use appropriate technological options for online technologies and course-related software, including Websites, e-mail, and online discussions for preparing the course and making it accessible to students.
• Model effective oral and written communications that engage the students, provide clarity, and improve student learning.
• Set clear expectations for the course by publishing course terminal objectives, assignment/examinations dates, and weight the distribution of various evaluation categories.
• Ensure that the content and level of material included on exams correspond to the course terminal objectives.
• Be available via email or telephone to provide support to the student.
• Introduce problem based learning presentations in which students are introduced to basic health assessment methods and tools.
• Facilitate discussions by asking questions, asking for rationale, and encouraging students to employ critical thinking skills as they encounter increasingly complex issues.
• Evaluate student progress in the effective use of critical thinking skills and the application of proficiencies developed in the program through practice exams.
• Communicate with students at least four times weekly throughout the 8-week course and respond to any student inquiries in a timely manner.
• We invite you to read our FAQ's about teaching for Chamberlain online for more details

You are encouraged to explore this opportunity if you meet these requirements:

• MSN and DNP (or MSN and PhD in nursing) degrees are required
• At least 1 year of practice experience directly in psychiatric mental health nursing is required
• Online Teaching experience is preferred (preferably at the graduate level)
• Must have active unencumbered RN nursing license; compact/multi-state licensure required

jobs.title: Print Production Intern (Winter/Spring 2027)
jobs.description:
About Formlabs:

A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.

Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.

That’s what we do.

At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

Your Impact:

As a Print Production Intern on our Sales Enablement Team, you will support our showroom and print production initiatives, including printer maintenance, SLA and SLS print production, and print farm clean-up and logistics to ensure a safe and inspiring environment to produce 3D printed solutions.

Internship Term: Winter/Spring 2027 (January 11 - April 30)
Commitment: Full-time (40 hours/week)
Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA (in-person)

The Job

• Support on design modifications, part layout and slicing for 3D print optimization.

• Support 3D print production including printing, troubleshooting and maintenance across SLA and SLS printers and all Formlabs materials.

• Post process, sand and finish parts.

• Support the team in space maintenance to ensure top of the line health and safety in the showroom and production spaces.

• Create and identify opportunities for space improvements to optimize production, printer utilization, quality control measures, and maintenance while ensuring health and safety of the space and everyone who uses it.

You

• Enjoy working independently.

• Are highly organized and interested in helping streamline processes.

• Have 3D printing experience and are motivated to become a 3D printing expert.

• Are Able to lift 40-80 lbs.

• Are eager to plug into the needs of the Sales team and the Formlabs community.

• Are confident working in Excel/Google Sheets and have a knack for Project Management.

Intern Benefits & Perks:

• Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it

• Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

• Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats

• Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns

• Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community

• And of course… unlimited 3D prints

You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

$1,000—$1,150 USD

jobs.title: Orthodox Rabbi at Harvard Hillel
jobs.description:
Orthodox Rabbi

Harvard Hillel

Role Overview

Harvard Hillel seeks a dynamic, relationship-centered, and intellectually curious Orthodox Rabbi to help shape a vibrant Orthodox Jewish community while contributing to the life of Harvard’s diverse Jewish community. This is an opportunity for a rabbi who loves Torah learning, cares deeply about students, and is excited to build meaningful relationships across differences in religious practice, belief, and background.

The ideal candidate will be a committed and inspiring exemplar of Torah and mitzvot, able to make Jewish tradition intellectually compelling, spiritually meaningful, and accessible to students with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. The rabbi will serve as a trusted teacher, mentor, and pastoral resource to Orthodox students while also building relationships with non-Orthodox students and contributing to a pluralistic Jewish community in which students can encounter different expressions of Jewish life with curiosity, respect, and a sense of belonging.

Working closely with students, student leaders, and Hillel colleagues, the rabbi will create opportunities for learning, Shabbat and holiday experiences, mentorship, and communal leadership. The successful candidate will be an inspiring Torah teacher and a relationship builder, showing a genuine desire to meet students where they are, engage their questions, and support them as they deepen their own Jewish lives.

At Harvard Hillel, a strong Orthodox community and a vibrant pluralistic Jewish community strengthen one another. We seek a rabbi who is confident and grounded in Orthodox practice, generous in relationships across differences, and eager to share the wisdom of Torah with students and colleagues throughout the Harvard community.

We welcome a candidate’s wife who is interested in helping build a vibrant Jewish community at Harvard to apply for a paid role as well. Depending on their interests and experience, this role might include learning with students, hosting Shabbat and holiday meals, building relationships, and planning and leading community programs. Our priority is to hire the strongest candidate for the role. At the same time, we recognize the potential value of a couple contributing to Jewish life at Harvard together, and welcome applications from couples interested in serving the community in complementary roles.

What You’ll Do

• Build relationships and provide pastoral care across the community: Develop meaningful relationships with Orthodox and non-Orthodox undergraduate and graduate students. Be a consistent, accessible presence in students’ lives, offering mentorship, pastoral care, and opportunities for Jewish learning and growth. Meet students where they are, without assumptions about their backgrounds, observance, beliefs, or prior Jewish learning.

• Teach Torah and contribute to a culture of learning: Teach Torah that is textually rigorous, intellectually ambitious, spiritually resonant, and responsive to students’ questions and interests. Create opportunities for sustained learning through shiurim, informal conversations, and regular chavruta study. Welcome challenging questions and foster a culture of learning characterized by curiosity, humility, and respect.

• Advise and develop the Orthodox Student Minyan: Serve as a trusted advisor to the Orthodox Student Minyan, offering shiurim, drashot, chavrutot, halakhic and hashkafic guidance, and practical organizational support. Partner with student leaders to cultivate a vibrant, welcoming minyan in which students take increasing ownership of communal life, religious practice, and programming.

• Contribute to pluralistic Jewish life at Harvard: Bring a confident Orthodox perspective to Harvard Hillel while actively engaging with students, rabbis, and colleagues from across the Jewish community. Participate in shared learning, programs, conversations, and communal gatherings, helping students encounter Jewish perspectives beyond their own and building relationships grounded in mutual respect. The rabbi should be able to articulate and share an Orthodox worldview while engaging thoughtfully and warmly with those who understand or practice Judaism differently.

• Create a home for Shabbat and holidays: Help students experience Shabbat and holidays as sources of connection, joy, spiritual depth, and community. Host students regularly in your home, collaborate with students and colleagues on meaningful holiday programming, and organize at least one off-site Shabbaton for the Orthodox community.

• Model exemplary middot: Relate to students and colleagues with warmth, care, humility, an approachability. Approach questions, disagreements, and conflicts with curiosity and a commitment to working toward solutions together. Be open to feedback and willing to consider others’ perspectives.

• Collaborate with the Hillel team: Work closely with the rabbinic and student life teams to develop and execute programs, support student-led initiatives, and advance shared engagement goals. Contribute ideas, follow through on commitments, communicate proactively, and help strengthen the team’s work.

• Partner with the broader Orthodox community: Serve as Harvard Hillel’s liaison to the broader Cambridge Orthodox Minyan at Harvard Hillel, supporting scheduling, financial coordination, and student participation in the broader Cambridge Orthodox community. Build relationships with local Jewish institutions and community partners to strengthen the experiences and resources available to students.

What You’ll Bring to the Job

• Strong Torah scholarship: Orthodox rabbinic ordination, deep textual knowledge, and the ability to teach traditional Jewish texts with rigor, creativity, and intellectual sophistication.

• Commitment to Orthodox Jewish life: A deep personal commitment to Torah, mitzvot, and the flourishing of Orthodox students and community.

• Excellence across differences: A genuine love of working with young adults and a demonstrated ability to build meaningful relationships with students across a wide range of Jewish backgrounds, practices, and perspectives.

• Pluralistic leadership: The ability to represent and teach from an Orthodox perspective while engaging non-Orthodox students and colleagues with warmth, curiosity, respect, and intellectual openness.

• Pastoral sensitivity: The ability to listen carefully, offer thoughtful guidance, navigate sensitive conversations, and support students through questions of identity, faith, relationships, and personal growth.

• Intellectual curiosity and humility: A willingness to ask questions before offering answers, acknowledge the limits of one’s knowledge, and continue learning alongside students and colleagues.

• Educational and programmatic skill: Experience designing, facilitating, and evaluating Jewish learning and community-building experiences. Experience in Hillel, experiential Jewish education, Orthodox communal settings, youth movements, or camp is valuable.

• Collaborative leadership: Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to work effectively with student leaders, colleagues, and community partners.

• A welcoming home: A willingness and ability to host students for Shabbat and holiday experiences.

• Professional qualifications: A bachelor’s degree, Orthodox rabbinic ordination, and membership in good standing in a rabbinic alumni association with established ethical guidelines.

What You’ll Receive

• Competitive salary of $135,000 for the rabbi role. If a spouse/partner is separately hired for a complementary role, that position carries an independent salary of up to $40,000.

• Comprehensive benefits, including health insurance, a tax-deferred retirement plan, life and disability insurance, a flex spending plan, generous vacation and sick time, and parental leave.

• A network of students, parents, university partners, and colleagues who will inspire you and become lifelong professional resources and partners.

• Opportunities for professional development, mentoring, and Jewish study.

• Colleagues and support from across the Hillel movement.

• Travel opportunities, both domestic and international.

• Stipends for Shabbat hosting experiences.

• Plenty of Hillel and university swag.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means that Orthodox students experience the minyan as a vibrant, welcoming, and student-owned community; students across Harvard’s Jewish community seek out the rabbi as a trusted teacher and mentor; Torah learning becomes a meaningful part of students’ lives; and the rabbi’s presence strengthens relationships, understanding, and shared Jewish life across differences. Success also means that the rabbi is a valued colleague across Harvard Hillel, contributing confidently from an Orthodox perspective while helping the broader Jewish community flourish.

About Harvard Hillel

Harvard Hillel is home to more than 500 Jewish undergraduates and 1,800 Jewish graduate students. Our mission is to help students build meaningful Jewish lives through relationships, learning, leadership, and community. Every member of our staff contributes to creating a welcoming environment where students can explore their identities, develop as leaders, and find a Jewish home on campus.

About Hillel International

In 1923, Rabbi Benjamin Frankel started Hillel with humble means, a noble mission and a breathtaking vision: to convey Jewish civilization to a new generation. Today, Hillel International continues to enrich the lives of Jewish students and is the largest Jewish campus organization in the world at nearly 1,000 colleges and universities across North America and around the world. As Hillel evolves as an organization, the mission remains steadfast: to create lasting connections with every Jewish student that foster an enduring commitment to Jewish life, learning, and Israel and train them to become the next Jewish leaders.

Hillel is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an accepting and inclusive environment for all.

jobs.title: Real Estate Associate
jobs.description:
About the Company:

Industrious is the largest premium workplace-as-a-service provider and home to the highest-rated workplaces in the industry. Everything we do comes down to creating great days for teams of all sizes and stages, including our own. We believe that what makes a great day at work is the people on your team and the problems you get to solve together. We’re looking for people who love thinking outside the box and thrive in a truly collaborative setting. As teammates, we encourage new ideas and toast every win. We’re excited about having a meaningful impact on people’s workplace experience.



Great days also start when everyone can be their authentic self at work. Diversity of backgrounds, thoughts, and ideas is critical to our success in delivering great workplace experiences, both for our members and for each other. Industrious is committed to creating an inclusive, respectful environment that embraces your individuality and quirkiness. You are valued for who YOU are. We celebrate our people as individuals who can accomplish great things when we work together as one team.



To learn more, visit www.industriousoffice.com/careers http://www.industriousoffice.com/careers.



About the Role

Industrious signs new landlord partnerships every year, and the number is growing as our business development team expands. Before any of those deals move forward, someone has to check that it holds together: that the assumptions are sound, that the start date, budgets, rent, pricing, and returns all track, and that the figures from design and construction have carried through correctly. As a Real Estate Associate on our Real Estate Transactions team that will be your job!



You will underwrite assigned deals in Excel, explain what drives their returns, and flag where a deal is tight, whether on pricing, occupancy, or CapEx. Our business development colleagues make the call on whether a deal goes ahead, and your analysis is what they rely on to make it well. You will work with Design, Construction, Finance, and other teams to make sure every number is right, supporting several business development colleagues as deal flow shifts.



Our approach to underwriting is different from a traditional real estate shop, and we will teach it to you. In your first few months you will get close review and clear guidance while you learn how we work. You will also join at a good time: the team is growing, new roles are being added, and we are underwriting a new product, so there is real room to learn, ask questions, and grow with us.



Success here means accurate work. The team trusts your numbers, your flags are clear, and any mistake you make happens once, not twice.



What Might Your Day Look Like

Your morning starts with a new deal from one of our business development colleagues. You go through the model piece by piece: the start date, the budget, the rent and revenue share assumptions, the cash flows, the IRR, and the margin the location is expected to earn per rentable square foot. The returns look fine at first, but pricing is tighter than it seems, so you note it clearly with the number that would need to change.



Late morning, updated figures arrive from Design and Construction. You check that they have flowed into the model correctly. One CapEx figure does not match the construction budget, so you confirm the right number with the construction team before it goes any further.



In the afternoon, you walk your business development colleague through the deal: what the returns look like, where the risk sits, and which assumptions matter most. They decide what happens next. Then priorities shift, and another colleague needs support on a deal heading to Investment Committee, so you move over and check that every figure in the review material ties back to the underwriting.



Before you wrap up, you update your trackers and checklists so the team knows where every deal you are supporting stands.



What You Will Own

 - Underwrite assigned deals in Excel, checking every assumption and making sure each component, from start date and budgets to pricing and IRR, tracks.

 - Explain each deal's returns clearly, including IRR, cash flows, P&L, and margin, so business development can make an informed decision.

 - Flag where a deal is tight, on pricing, occupancy, CapEx, OpEx, rent, or revenue share, and where it may need more support.

 - Make sure figures from Design, Construction, and Finance carry through accurately into the deal.

 - Support deal reviews and Investment Committee materials with numbers that hold up to scrutiny.

 - Support several business development colleagues across their deal flow, moving between priorities as needs change.

 - Keep the trackers and checklists that help the team stay accurate as deal volume grows.
   
   

You Will Love This Role If...

 - You are curious about real estate and want to understand why a deal works, not just what the model says.

 - Getting it right matters more to you than getting it fast, and when you make a mistake, you build a check so it does not happen again. That is Drives Excellence (#hands) in practice.

 - You enjoy tracing a problem to its source: which variable breaks the deal, and what would need to be true for it to work. That is Problem Solving (#head).

 - You can explain a model in plain terms, so colleagues understand the conclusion without having to decode the spreadsheet. That is Communication (#heart).

 - You adapt well when priorities change, and you are comfortable supporting several colleagues at once.

 - You want to learn a new approach to underwriting on a growing team where there is room to develop.
   
   

This Role Is Probably Not for You If...

 - You want to make the final call on deals yourself. Business development owns that decision, and your role is to make sure it is well informed.

 - You find detailed checking draining. This role covers a high volume of deals, and the standard is accuracy every time.

 - You prefer settled processes. We are underwriting a new product, so some of how we work is still taking shape, and priorities can move quickly.

 - You prefer to work on your own. Much of the role depends on working with other teams, managing expectations, and meeting shared deadlines.
   
   

What We Are Looking For

 - Strong Excel skills: IRR and time value of money, financial statements, EBITDA, pivot tables, and Goal Seek, with the ability to explain how a model works and why each piece fits.

 - Hands-on experience analyzing or underwriting deals, ideally in real estate, or in finance with a genuine interest in real estate.

 - A track record of accurate work across a high volume of tasks, with work that holds up to review.

 - A record of working well across teams, managing expectations, and delivering to deadlines.

 - Nice to have: exposure to leases, landlords, or office and flexible workspace, and progress toward a designation such as the CFA or CPA. You do not need Argus or prior knowledge of our underwriting approach.
   
   

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary for this role is $110,000 - $120,000, depending on experience, skills, and role alignment. This role is also eligible for an annual bonus and participation in our long-term incentive program. But compensation is only part of the story.



At Industrious, we believe a good workplace supports the whole person. Not just the work they do. Our benefits are designed to give people the stability, flexibility, and room to grow that make a career sustainable.



Our benefits include:

 - Heavily subsidized medical, dental, and vision plans to support you and your family

 - Flexible paid time off, to maintain balance

 - Paid parental leave to help you welcome a new child and focus on what matters most

 - Annual professional development grants so you can keep learning and growing

 - 401(k) retirement savings program to support long-term financial wellbeing

 - Wellness initiatives and additional employee support programs
   
   

Specific benefits may vary by role, location, and eligibility requirements.



Industrious has been recognized by Built In as a Best Place to Work across multiple major markets. Not because of one office or one team, but because people across the company help make this a place where work feels human.



If you are curious about real estate and care about getting the numbers right, we would love to hear from you. Our process includes an Excel underwriting case that you will present and talk through, so you can show us how you think.



Equal Employment Opportunity: Industrious is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity. We have a long-standing commitment to providing equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, veteran status, political belief, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
The Behavior team at Motional is responsible for developing the prediction, planning, and sim agent capabilities that enable our autonomous vehicles to navigate complex, dynamic environments safely, comfortably, and confidently. Our work spans understanding and anticipating the behavior of other road users, making intelligent driving decisions, and generating safe, efficient, and natural vehicle trajectories. We combine cutting-edge machine learning, robotics, large-scale data, and rigorous evaluation to advance the capabilities of our production autonomous driving system.

We are looking for a highly motivated, technically strong engineer to lead evaluation initiatives across Prediction and Planning. In this role, you will define how we measure, understand, and improve autonomous driving behavior, bridging the gap between individual model performance and real-world system outcomes. You will drive the development of advanced evaluation methodologies, performance metrics, data mining strategies, and scalable tools to identify system limitations, assess dataset coverage, and guide model development.

You will work closely with machine learning engineers, roboticists, safety, and cross-functional teams to tackle challenging, open-ended problems and establish the quantitative foundations that drive improvements in safety, comfort, and driving performance. Your work will directly influence how we develop, evaluate, and deploy the next generation of autonomous driving capabilities.

What You’ll Do

• Act as the central authority on evaluation for our Behaviors teams, bridging the gap between model development and system-level autonomous behavior.

• Drive the evaluation strategy for our prediction and planning models, including open-loop and simulation-based assessments.

• Design and implement advanced metrics to measure model impact on overall system behavior, leveraging ML-based approaches for robust, end-to-end model evaluation.

• Incorporate concepts such as counterfactual reasoning and reaction time analysis into our evaluation frameworks to better understand system behavior.

• Develop the strategy for data mining and assess the coverage of our training and evaluation datasets across Prediction and Planning.

• Build necessary tooling and pipelines, identify gaps in our processes, and collaborate with machine learning engineers and roboticists to solve open-ended problems.

• Cross-functional collaboration: Partner with Safety, Infrastructure, Operations, Legal, and the other Systems teams to drive design improvements and ensure features generate a net positive effect on system safety, comfort, and assertiveness and meet our launch criteria.

What We’re Looking For:

• Bachelor’s degree and 7+ years of experience in Computer Science, Systems Engineering, Robotics, or a similar technical field (or Master’s/PhD and 5+ years of experience).

• Strong foundation in probability/statistics, data science, and scientific rigor applied to complex, multi-agent systems.

• Proficiency in Python, SQL, and data analysis (visualization, statistics) in production environments.

• Experience defining performance targets and acceptance criteria spanning safety, comfort, and assertiveness, producing the analysis and evidence to justify them.

• Demonstrated ability to tackle technical challenges, analyze cross-disciplinary problems, and propose innovative, maintainable solutions.

• Proven ability to lead initiatives, drive alignment, and ensure stakeholder engagement throughout the development process.

• Working expertise in hazard and safety analysis methods such as STPA, HAZOP, FMEA, and hazard analysis and risk assessment.

Ideally, You Also Have:

• Experience using statistical and ML methods to quantify performance, detect regressions, and reveal patterns of system behavior at scale.

• Deep experience with Prediction and/or Planning for autonomous robotics, including evaluating ML-based systems in production environments.

• Experience with public AV datasets and benchmarks (e.g., Waymo Open Dataset, nuScenes, etc.) and a deep understanding of standard industry metrics for trajectory forecasting and motion planning.

• Prior experience using or building data pipelines at scale.

• Excellent communication skills, capable of articulating complex concepts to technical peers and executive leadership alike, with a proven ability to collaborate across distributed teams.

• Familiarity with SOTIF, ISO 26262, UL4600, and AVSC behavior competencies and other industry standards.

• A True Hunter: You genuinely enjoy prospecting, negotiating and winning new business, and you're comfortable breaking into accounts where you have no existing relationships.

• Product & Demo Enthusiasm: You enjoy learning the product and running multiple targeted demos. You’re confident tailoring walkthroughs to prospect needs and using the product to drive discovery and deal progression, rather than relying heavily on an SE.

• Self-Generated Pipeline: A consistent history of building your own pipeline through outbound prospecting, networking and account penetration, rather than relying on inbound or BDR-sourced opportunities.

• Deal Execution: Excellent at discovery, multi-threading and navigating complex, multi-stakeholder buying processes. Comfortable guiding customers through security and compliance reviews.

• Operational Rigor: You run your territory like your own business. CRM discipline, accurate forecasting, pipeline management and deal inspection are second nature

• Tools and Methodology: Proficiency with Salesforce (or similar CRM) and established sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC.

• A Builder's Mindset: Proven success in a startup, scale-up or similarly high-growth environment. You're energized by building something rather than inheriting it.

• Hunger and Accountability: You're commercially ambitious, competitive, resilient, curious and highly accountable, with a strong sense of urgency. You're coachable and collaborative, but you don't need to be pushed into action.

Strongly Preferred:

None of the following are required, but they will set you apart. Candidates who bring one or more of them will receive strong preference, especially when combined with the SaaS sales track record described above.

• Proposal Experience: Hands-on experience in proposal management, proposal writing, capture or bid management in Federal, SLED, commercial or AEC markets. Having sat in our customers' seats is a significant advantage in this role.

• Shipley Training: Formal Shipley training (for example, proposal management, capture management or the Business Development Lifecycle) and fluency in Shipley best practices.

• APMP Certification: APMP Foundation, Practitioner or Professional certification.

• GovCon Fluency: Experience selling into US Government Contractors or a strong working knowledge of the Federal/GovCon market.

Also Valued:

• Education: Bachelor's degree preferred. Candidates without a degree will be considered where they have a strong record of success in complex B2B sales, business development, proposal and/or capture roles.

Compensation and Benefits:

• Competitive Salary: $120,000 - $140,000 base (50/50 commission split, up to $280,000 OTE uncapped)

• Stock Options: Meaningful equity in the company.

• Comprehensive medical/dental/life insurance: Insurance coverage for individuals and families partially paid by the company as well as opportunity to participate in pre-tax health Flexible Spending Account.

• Retirement Plan: Ability to invest your pre-tax dollars in a 401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions.

• Paid Time Off: Unlimited vacation (Yes, you read right!)

• Flexible Work Options: Based in DC/Northern Virginia with regular travel to NYC and customer events required.

• Paid parental leave: 12 weeks if you’ve just given birth, 4 weeks if your partner has just given birth (after one year of service)

• Additional Perks: Your choice of laptop (Mac or Windows), regular company events to connect with teammates, and opportunities for continued professional development.

Values in Action:

These aren’t just principles we print and forget – they’re how we work, how we treat each other, and how we deliver for our customers. They shape the company we are, and the one we aspire to become.

• Customers, Always: Everything starts with our customers. We walk in their shoes, speak their language, and build for their delight and success. We win when they win.

• Make It Happen: We move fast and take ownership. No waiting, no red tape – just action, urgency, and focus on outcomes.

• Learn and Invent: We stay curious. We learn what we can from past masters - and make up the rest. Change is constant, and so is our growth.

• Act Like Owners: Titles don’t solve problems - people do. We own challenges, break the rules when it’s necessary, and focus on what matters.

• Turn It Up to 11: There is no “Good enough”. We raise the bar, push boundaries, and keep building. There’s always a next level.

• Lead With Respect: We listen first, speak honestly, and value every perspective. Integrity, follow-through, and kindness matter.

• Build Trust Through Transparency: We default to openness. We give feedback, share information, and assume positive intent - no secrets, no silos.

Certified Dispense & Fill Pharmacy Technician Pay Rate: $24/hr

 - Assist as-needed in maintenance of pharmacy inventory by checking stock to determine inventory level, anticipating needed medications and supplies, placing and expediting orders, verifying receipt, and removing outdated drugs

 - Maintain a safe pharmacy environment by complying with standard operating procedures, rules, and regulations

 - Clean and help maintain pharmacy areas, pharmacy equipment and work areas as directed by standard operating procedures. 

 - Transition medications through various states of workflow

 - Protect patients and employees by adhering to strict infection-control policies and protocols.

 - Contribute to team effort by accomplishing related results as needed

 - Ability to work flexible shift times

 - Attention to detail

 - Willingness to work in a team environment and promote company culture

 - Proficiency in English, verbal and written

 - Proficiency in Windows based computer systems

 - Experience working in a community, mail-order, or hospital pharmacy as a registered pharmacy technician is a plus

 - Affordable medical, dental & vision insurance

 - Robust employee leave policies, including PTO, holidays, and family leave

 - 401k with employer contribution

 - Pet insurance

 - and more!

 

Conditions of Employment: 

 - This position will require working with Hazardous Drugs (HD) and would require that Personal Protective Equipmemnt (PPE) be worn for the length of working with these drugs. These items would include gloves, respiratory protection, gown and other items as required.

 - This position requires medical approval to wear respiratory protection in the form of negative or positive pressure respirators, including N95, full face respirator, SCBA, or Powered Air Purifying Respirator (PAPR).

 - Physical exertion required. Including, but not limited to, walking up to 50% of the time, standing up to 100% of the time, squatting and bending up to 20% of the time and lifting up to 80% of the time for up to a twelve hour shift. Must be able to lift up to 50lbs.

jobs.title: Customer Adoption Consultant
jobs.description:
Role Purpose

The Customer Adoption Consultant helps customers successfully onboard, use and realise value from IFS.ai Logistics. Working within the adoption operating model and with coaching from a Customer Adoption Manager, the Consultant coordinates customer activities, maintains delivery discipline, analyses adoption signals, delivers training and turns customer feedback into clear actions. The scope is narrower than the Manager role, with defined accounts or workstreams and clear escalation for complex commercial, executive or delivery decisions.

Key Accountabilities

1. Deliver Structured Customer Onboarding

• Coordinate assigned customer onboarding activities from handover through first value, using agreed playbooks, templates and governance.

• Prepare kick-off materials, project plans, action trackers, weekly updates, meeting notes, risk logs and customer documentation.

• Run working-level customer meetings and follow-ups; keep owners, dependencies and deadlines visible and accurate.

• Coordinate customer data, provider and workflow inputs with Product Operations and technical teams, escalating quality or readiness risks early.

2. Enable Product Adoption

• Help translate customer goals into practical use cases, learning plans, milestones and measures of success.

• Deliver or coordinate product training, enablement sessions, SOPs and point-of-need guidance.

• Monitor usage, engagement and completion of agreed activities; follow up on barriers and recommend interventions.

• Support customers in embedding the platform into routine logistics, finance and operational workflows.

3. Maintain Customer Health and Value Evidence

• Maintain accurate account records, adoption metrics, health signals, progress updates and value evidence in agreed systems.

• Analyse customer feedback, product usage and operational information to identify risks, needs and improvement opportunities.

• Prepare materials for adoption reviews and executive meetings, including progress, outcomes, risks, actions and next steps.

• Capture customer quotes, proof points, success stories and referenceability signals with appropriate approval.

4. Support Retention, Expansion and Product Feedback

• Surface adoption risks and contribute to recovery plans under the direction of the Customer Adoption Manager or account owner.

• Identify potential expansion opportunities from workflow gaps, customer requests and underused or adjacent capabilities, then route them to the appropriate lead.

• Gather structured customer feedback and translate it into clear evidence for Product, Engineering and operational teams.

• Support feature validation, user acceptance activity and post-release feedback for assigned customers.

5. Improve the Adoption Practice

• Keep playbooks, templates, SOPs and knowledge assets accurate and up to date.

• Contribute lessons learned from customer engagements and suggest practical improvements to processes and automation.

• Apply consistent quality, data governance and documentation standards across assigned work.

• Build product and logistics domain knowledge and share learning with colleagues.

Experience and Capabilities

Essential

• Approximately two or more years of experience in B2B SaaS customer success, onboarding, implementation, consulting, project coordination, product operations or a related customer-facing role.

• Strong organisation and follow-through, with the ability to manage actions, deadlines, documentation and multiple stakeholders.

• Clear written and verbal communication and confidence facilitating working sessions with customers.

• Comfort using data and customer evidence to monitor progress, identify issues and prepare concise updates.

• Customer-focused problem solving with the judgement to resolve routine issues and escalate material risks appropriately.

• Good Excel capability and confidence learning SaaS platforms, collaboration tools and operational workflows.

• Ability to work across teams and maintain accuracy in a fast-moving environment.

Desirable

• Experience in logistics, transport, supply chain, freight audit, finance operations or another complex enterprise process.

• Experience delivering software training, adoption activities or change communications.

• Exposure to product analytics, BI tools, SQL or structured data validation.

• Experience working with AI-enabled software or explaining analytical outputs to users.

jobs.title: H&M Department Manager - Northpark Mall
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Department Manager, you’ll be the leader supporting and encouraging your whole team. By bringing everyone together, you’ll be able to create an inclusive culture that promotes collaboration and an entrepreneurial spirit, helping you, your team, and H&M succeed. Ensuring an excellent operational & visual experience for your store, customers & colleagues. You’ll be aware of your store’s strengths, opportunities, and competitors. Analyze and follow up on sales, and create plans to optimize results and profits.

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Customer Sales & Profit

• You are responsible for the total OMNI customer experience in your store, ensuring visual and commercial curation according to global guidelines
• Representing yourself and the H&M brand positively during customer interactions
• Be aware of and take responsibility of your department's strengths and identifying commercial opportunities and acting on them
• Establish & analyze sales and budget goals, creating plans to optimize results
• Ensure customer service is provided in all areas of the store and that your team has the ability to work towards actively promoting and selling products to customers
• Following up that your team is actively promoting our Customer Loyalty App (Hello Member) & in-store sustainability initiatives
• Manage your department in a cost-efficient way
• Ensure correct routines in fitting room and checkout, including transaction, returns and exchanges
• Ensure all admin routines for both people and operations are handled in a correct way

Fashion & Trend Awareness

• Keep up-to-date with fashion scene, trends, tendencies, styles, brands, products, competitors and relevant influencers, etc
• Ensure your team provides product and fashion knowledge as well as other relevant information during customer interactions

Team & Development

• Responsible for recruitment, onboarding, performance management, upskilling & developing your team in-store
• Complete performance evaluations and succession planning to support business & team needs
• Retain and share your knowledge and skills with your team
• Collaboration, planning & teamwork with in-store Visual Merchandiser team
• Give & receive feedback with your colleagues to learn, develop & support each other
• Responsible for the teams planning & scheduling
• Regular communication to store colleagues to inform, motivate and inspire – daily, weekly meetings, etc
• Ensure all procedures, routines, and legal requirements in all areas of the store are followed
• Participate in relevant available Onboarding & introduction processes, trainings and courses relevant for your role & future development

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

• Secure a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house including stockroom areas
• Ensure high fashion quality, visual and commercial product presentation, with good garment care
• Secure good stock levels and provide input on allocation to Area team
• Ensure the full garment cycle – from delivery to garment presentation – and fitting room routines are according to our standards and routines set internally, utilizing all tools and technology provided
• Upkeep & follow best practice for any in-store OMNI Services & in-store tech services/tools, etc (Instore Care App, Click & Collect, Smart Store etc)
• Secure a strong balance and the maintenance of price signs in-store and throughout the sales floor/store following guidelines according to global and local strategies & sales market/regional requirements to ensure a strong and consistent price perception throughout store
• Updating & upkeep of BOH Areas for all colleagues (key information, health & safety, tidiness etc)
• Responsible for opening & closing of store daily

Who You Are

• To be a successful and effective Department Manager, you’ll be a strong leader who enjoys taking responsibility for others.
• You must be ambitious, an effective communicator, supportive, an analytical solution finder, capable of working with numbers and managing statistics.
• You are achievement-oriented, motivated by performance and competition to be truly customer centric.

Why You’ll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years
• You’ll have access to our Colleague Resource Groups (CRGs) to find community and networking opportunities among colleagues

jobs.description:

About You

As an Account Manager Associate at Broker Online Exchange, you will be a part of our sales team. You will manage brokerage partners and advisors, building strong relationships with these partners, and assisting them with everything they need from pricing and contracting to helping aspiring partners learn the industry. You will become an expert in the deregulated energy market and develop partnerships, increasing business revenue. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, client-facing environment, and is a proactive initiator.

What you'll do and how you'll have an impact

• Collaborate cross-functionally with internal teams, including operations, pricing, and supplier partners, to deliver a smooth experience from initial quote to completed contract.

• Participate in occasional travel, meetings, or hosted events to strengthen partner relationships and deepen market understanding.

• Grow your career in Account Management, gaining the experience and exposure needed to advance into more senior roles as the department continues to expand.

What We're Looking For

• Strong relationship-building abilities, capable of fostering trust, credibility, and long-term partnerships.

Broker Online Exchange, an AppDirect Company, is committed to fostering a healthy work–life balance that supports both individual performance and strong team collaboration. Our organization has continued to evolve with resilience, creating an environment where employees can thrive professionally while maintaining flexibility in their personal lives.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Athletic Development Intern

Reports to: Director of Sports Performance / Strength & Conditioning Coach

Department: Sports Performance

Position Summary:

This internship provides the opportunity to gain knowledge and experience working in a professional soccer organization. The strength and conditioning intern position will assist staff supporting FCC and FCC2 players. This position will be based out of the Mercy Health Training Center in Milford, Ohio. The schedule is Monday - Friday with the possibility of weekend sessions, working an average of 20 hours a week. This is an hourly paid position.

Please note this position is allotted for the 2027 MLS Sprint Season, which runs from February through April. However, there may be an opportunity for continued employment during the 2027–2028 season based on organizational needs and individual performance.

What You’ll Do:

• Assist Physical Development Coach with FCC2 athlete preparation, end-stage rehabilitation, and injury prevention in close communication with management, coaching and medical staff.

• Upskill in strength and power assessment technologies to provide strength and conditioning assessments for soccer players. Work with staff to perform a needs analysis of each player to identify individual strengths and weakness and drive appropriate individual development

• Support the strength & conditioning strategies of FCC and FCC2 players in accordance with scientific training principles.

• Support the delivery of gym and field-based strength and conditioning support programs to players

• Support the Strength & Conditioning Coach in the delivery of pre-training activation sessions and lead on the delivery of activation sessions to FCC2 players.

• Utilize technologies to collect, analyze and feedback gym-based player

• Support staff with equipment set-up and clearance for team-based and individual

What You’ll Bring:

• Willingness to learn and receive feedback

• Creative, dynamic, and enthusiastic personality

• Excellent organizational and time-management skills

• Ability to demonstrate appropriately with a motivational coaching style

• Ability to collaborate successfully as part of a Multi-Disciplinary Team to solve performance problems

• Enrolled in an Exercise Science undergraduate program

jobs.title: Director, Financial Systems & Transformation
jobs.location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is building the payment layer for life's financial obligations, giving households one place to see, split, and pay their bills around how they live and get paid. By offering greater choice over how and when payments are made and allowing eligible on time payments to help build a positive credit history, Flex puts households back in control of their cash flow.

That work brings together people with different perspectives who challenge the status quo and take ownership of solving difficult problems. For you, that means doing the best work of your career next to people who make you better, and together bringing ideas to life that make a real impact for the people we serve.

About the Role

We are seeking a strategic leader who pairs deep systems expertise with strong process design instincts to build and own Flex's Financial Systems & Transformation function from the ground up. This is a rare opportunity to define a new pillar within the Finance organization at a fast-scaling fintech — one where the scope extends well beyond traditional ERP administration into agentic AI infrastructure, process automation, and the controls architecture that will underpin Flex’s next phase of growth.

As Director, Financial Systems & Transformation, you will own the internal financial systems that power Flex’s accounting and financial reporting function — including our core ERP, procure-to-pay (P2P), T&E systems, and additional financial reporting tooling as the function matures. You will also design, build, and maintain the AI-powered workflows that are central to Flex’s vision for a modern, scalable Finance function, and you will lead the build-out of ITGC and financial systems controls that keep pace with the business as it scales.

This role sits at the intersection of finance, systems, and AI — and requires a leader who can operate with fluency across all three. You will partner closely with the VP Controller, the broader Finance leadership team, and Flex’s Engineering and AI Central teams to make the vision real. This position will be based in our New York headquarters on a hybrid basis and will report to the VP Controller.

What You'll Do

Financial Systems Ownership & Administration

• Own our ERP (Campfire) as Flex’s financial system of record — including configuration, close module setup, chart of accounts and dimension/segment governance, and ongoing system health

• Own our procure-to-pay (P2P) systems for AP and T&E — evaluating near-term enhancements and long-term tooling strategy as we scale

• Manage integrations between core financial systems and the upstream/downstream data sources that feed them — including the payroll (Rippling) integration in partnership with the People/HRIS systems team — ensuring accurate, timely, and auditable data flows across the Finance stack

• Serve as the internal product owner for financial systems enhancements — translating Finance team requirements into system configuration and working with vendors and technical teams where needed

• Partner with the Strategic Finance team on the evaluation, implementation, and ongoing administration of FP&A tooling, supporting both the Finance and business planning functions

• Evaluate, implement, and administer additional tooling across Finance as the function scales — including financial reporting, SOX, and account reconciliations

Agentic AI Infrastructure

• Design, build, and maintain AI-powered workflows that eliminate manual, high-volume processes across the Finance function — with a particular focus on transaction coding, close automation, and financial reporting

• Own the technical architecture for agent-as-preparer workflows: defining confidence thresholds and exception routing, and building the audit trail infrastructure required in a controls-conscious environment

• Partner with Flex’s AI Central team to extend our internal AI platform into Finance use cases — including inquiry triage, routing, and other templatable workflows

• Proactively identify and prioritize new automation opportunities across the Accounting & Finance function; own the agentic build roadmap in partnership with Finance leadership

• Establish and maintain operational health monitoring for all automated workflows — exception rates, throughput metrics, and escalation paths

ITGC, Access Controls & Controls Readiness

• Own IT General Controls (ITGCs) across all financial systems — user access provisioning and deprovisioning, segregation of duties (SOD) enforcement, change management controls, and periodic access reviews

• Design and maintain the control framework and access architecture for automated/agentic workflows — including permissioning, auditability, and documentation standards for a future SOX-ready environment

• Build out Flex’s broader controls readiness over time — ITGC documentation, control testing support, and GRC tool implementation as the company scales

• Serve as the primary liaison between the Finance function and external auditors on technology-related matters, including audit trail standards and controls evidence for automated workflows

Close Automation & Process Optimization

• Build and maintain real-time close monitoring: dashboards and alerts that give Finance leadership live visibility into close status, open items, and risk flags

• Partner with the VP Controller to systematically accelerate the month-end close cycle — identifying and removing structural bottlenecks through better tooling, automation, and process design

• Support the build-out of automated financial reporting infrastructure — enabling reliable, timely reporting across P&L, balance sheet, cash flow, and operational metrics with minimal manual intervention

• Drive P2P process optimization and efficiency — implementing system-based workflows, reducing processing and cycle time, and continuously improving the AP and T&E experience across Finance and the broader company

Team & Stakeholder Leadership

• Build out and shape the Financial Systems & Transformation function over time — defining scope, identifying capability gaps, and bringing in talent as the function evolves

• Serve as the Finance function’s primary technical voice in cross-functional forums — partnering with Engineering, Product, Data, and AI Central on decisions that affect financial data, systems, and processes

• Champion AI and systems adoption across the Finance team — providing training, tooling guidance, and hands-on support to help Finance professionals get the most out of available tools

What We're Looking For

Required

• 10+ years of experience in financial systems, accounting technology, or a closely related field — with meaningful time spent in a high-growth or scaling environment

• Deep ERP expertise — ideally including implementation experience (go-live, integration design, configuration, and post-live optimization) with platforms such as NetSuite, Campfire, Sage Intacct, or equivalent

• Strong finance and accounting foundation — sufficient understanding of US GAAP, month-end close processes, and financial reporting to both translate business requirements into systems design and identify where process redesign itself is the better answer, without losing fidelity

• Demonstrated experience building or owning IT General Controls and access control frameworks — SOD enforcement, user provisioning, change management, and audit-trail documentation

• Strong grasp of financial master data design and governance — chart of accounts structure, dimension/segment design, and the data architecture decisions that determine downstream reporting flexibility

• Demonstrated ability to design or re-engineer core accounting processes (close, AP, payroll, or similar) around best practices — not just automate existing process but rethink it

• Experience working directly with external auditors (Big 4 preferred) on IT controls testing and audit evidence standards

• Hands-on experience with API integrations and data pipeline design — comfort working with Engineering teams to scope and spec integration work

• Genuine enthusiasm for AI and automation — you think naturally about where agent-based workflows can replace manual processes, and you’re excited to build them

• Exceptional communication skills — ability to translate between finance, engineering, and executive audiences without oversimplifying or losing technical precision

• Comfort building and scaling in a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment — this is very much a “build the plane while flying it” role, and success will depend on strong prioritization instincts and the ability to move quickly as priorities shift

Strongly Preferred

• Experience with Campfire or another AI-native ERP platform — distinct from legacy systems, these environments call for a different way of thinking about configuration and workflow design

• Experience designing or operating AI-automated workflows in a finance or accounting context — intelligent document processing, transaction coding automation, or similar

• SOX compliance experience, including ITGC documentation, RCM design, and internal or external audit support — ideally in a pre-IPO or newly public company

• Experience with close management platforms (FloQast, BlackLine, or equivalent) and financial reporting automation tooling

• Prior experience at a fintech, payments company, or similarly regulated financial services environment

• CPA or equivalent credential is a plus, not a requirement

• Formal project management experience or training — this role requires running complex, cross-functional projects to completion, not just providing technical and functional expertise

• Experience leading close process optimization or standardization initiatives, ideally reducing close timelines or manual touch-points

• Familiarity with payroll and AP operational best practices — vendor management, payment controls, exception handling — beyond the systems that support them

Compensation

Flex takes a market-based approach to pay, ensuring compensation is commensurate with a candidate's experience and our internal leveling guidelines. For candidates located in our Tier 1 (NYC/Bay Area) and Tier 3 (Salt Lake City) markets, the base salary pay range for this role is below. Flex utilizes a geographic pay differential based on a cost of labor index. If you are located outside of the cities listed below, your starting pay will be adjusted to align with the market conditions of your specific geographic zone. Please speak with your recruiter for additional information regarding the specific range for your location.

Tier 1 (NYC/Bay Area)

$180,000—$225,000 USD

Tier 3 (Salt Lake City)

$150,000—$190,000 USD

Life at Flex

Building a successful company takes a diverse team of intelligent, curious, determined, empathetic, and self-aware people. Our headquarters is in New York City, with employees across the US, Australia, Canada, and South America. We’re growing quickly and deliberately, with a focus on building an inclusive culture. We value the perspectives our people bring and take pride in being an equal opportunity workplace.

Offices

Roles posted in New York, San Francisco, and Salt Lake City are hybrid positions with on-site expectations of 2-3 days per week in our local offices. For candidates outside of these areas, you may be eligible for our relocation assistance program.

Benefits

View our benefits and more at getflex.com/careers.

jobs.title: Sr. Production Broadcast Engineer - NBC Sports
jobs.description:
The Senior Broadcast Production Engineer is a highly experienced technical contributor responsible for maintaining the reliability of NBC Sports production environments while leading complex troubleshooting, systems design, integration and technology projects. This role serves as a senior escalation point for live productions and provides technical leadership across studios, production control rooms and associated broadcast and IP infrastructure within the Stamford Sports facility.

The Senior Broadcast Production Engineer partners with Production, Operations, Technical Management, IT, Security, vendors and other engineering teams to translate production requirements into reliable and supportable technical solutions. The position combines hands-on day-of-air support with systems engineering, project leadership, operational readiness and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

• Serve as a senior technical escalation point for complex or high-impact issues affecting live and recorded productions.
• Lead advanced troubleshooting across video, audio, communications, replay, graphics, routing, monitoring, compute, storage and network-connected production systems.
• Provide senior day-of-air engineering coverage and coordinate technical response during production-impacting incidents.
• Lead technical projects from requirements definition and design through installation, integration, testing, commissioning and operational handoff.
• Develop system architecture, signal-flow diagrams, equipment specifications, implementation plans and acceptance criteria.
• Evaluate existing workflows and recommend improvements that increase reliability, scalability, security and operational efficiency.
• Lead maintenance windows, system upgrades, capacity expansions and technology refreshes while minimizing production disruption.
• Work with Network Engineering and IT teams to support IP media environments, including SMPTE ST 2110, multicast transport, synchronization and hybrid SDI/IP workflows.
• Coordinate technical work performed by system integrators, manufacturers and vendors; validate deliverables and oversee acceptance testing.
• Perform root-cause analysis following significant incidents and translate findings into corrective actions, documentation or system improvements.
• Develop and maintain engineering standards, SOPs, as-built drawings, recovery procedures and technical support documentation.
• Mentor less-experienced engineers and provide technical training and knowledge sharing.
• Represent Production Engineering in cross-functional project, workflow and technology discussions.
• Support budgeting, equipment planning and technical lifecycle recommendations for assigned systems.
• Participate in rotating schedule and on-call coverage, including nights, weekends and holidays as required.

Basic Requirements

• Minimum five years of progressively responsible experience in broadcast engineering, production engineering, media systems or a comparable live-production technology environment.
• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Communications or a related field, or equivalent relevant education and experience.
• Demonstrated expertise troubleshooting integrated broadcast production systems in high-pressure, time-sensitive environments.
• Experience leading system installations, upgrades, integration, testing or commissioning.
• Strong knowledge of video, audio, timing, synchronization, signal transport, monitoring and production control-room workflows.
• Strong understanding of IP networking and media-over-IP production technologies.
• Experience creating and maintaining system diagrams, technical specifications and operational documentation.
• Demonstrated ability to lead technical workstreams and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Desired Characteristics

• Experience with SMPTE ST 2110, PTP, NMOS, AES67, Dante, NDI and hybrid SDI/IP production environments.
• Experience with redundant, highly available systems supporting 24/7 media operations.
• Familiarity with cloud, virtualized or software-defined production platforms.
• Experience with Sony, EVS, Evertz, Grass Valley, RTS, Calrec, Tektronix, Leader, Avid and Chyron systems.
• Experience with 1080p, HDR and UHD/4K workflows.
• Experience using AutoCAD, Visio, Lucidchart or similar tools for systems documentation.
• Familiarity with scripting, automation, monitoring or configuration-management tools.
• Experience managing vendor deliverables and formal system acceptance testing.
• Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers and improve team support practices.
• Strong ownership mindset, judgment and composure during production-critical incidents.

Additional Requirements

• Willingness to work overtime, including nights and weekends.
• Must be willing to work in Stamford, CT.
• Must be willing to submit to a background investigation.
• Must have unrestricted work authorization to work in the United States.
• It is the policy of NBCUniversal and NBCUniversal’ s affiliated businesses to consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex (including pregnancy) sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, or other characteristics protected by law.

This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: $63.00 - $68.00 per hour.
